topology_reasoning.operation: Each cardinal single-mode access waveguide broadens smoothly into a compact central crossing region. The four rotationally symmetric lobes create gradual mode expansion and recompression instead of an abrupt orthogonal intersection.
topology_reasoning.observed_geometry: The calibrated 4.7 um square contains four equal narrow ports, each about 0.55 um long, followed by a teardrop-shaped lobe. The lobes are widest before the center and taper into a merged central region.
topology_reasoning.implementation: One arm is assembled from a straight and two sine-width gf.Path transition extrusions, then rotated four times. This uses only primitive geometry and naturally merges the overlapping central lobes. delta_length is a real narrow-guide path extension used for the parametric response proof.

iterations.change_made: Initial four-arm sine-transition crossing; the rotational placement inadvertently put each broad lobe at the outside and left the center underfilled.
Reduced lobe_max_width from 1.72 um to 0.94 um and center_width to 0.78 um after measuring the target cross-sections.
Tested a longer expansion and shorter contraction; the metric declined, so this profile was rejected.
Restored the better 0.95/0.85 um lobe profile and anchored each arm's central end at the common crossing center; this corrected the reversed lobe orientation.
